samples.question: The picture shows identical coloured dots placed on the sites of an evenly spaced square grid, except that some sites are empty. A grid line is a whole row of sites, a whole column of sites, a diagonal of sites running down to the right, or a diagonal of sites running up to the right. Exactly one grid line has more empty sites than every other grid line, and no two empty sites on that line are next to each other. The dot colour, the background colour, the dot size, the grid spacing, the grid size, the position of the grid and the total number of empty sites carry no information about the answer. Which direction does that line run? Answer row (horizontal), column (vertical), down (diagonal running down to the right) or up (diagonal running up to the right).
